question: A mother asks why her 3-month-old breastfed infant seems to need feeding so frequently compared to her older child. Which statement best explains the energy requirement pattern across paediatric age groups?

answers.text: Energy requirements per kilogram are lowest in early infancy and rise progressively through adolescence.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The pattern is the reverse — requirements per kilogram are highest in early infancy and decline progressively as growth velocity decreases.

answers.text: Energy requirements per kilogram are highest in early infancy and decline progressively as growth velocity decreases.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Infants have the highest energy requirements per kilogram due to rapid growth and a proportionally larger brain metabolic demand. This is why frequent feeding is normal in early infancy.

answers.text: Energy requirements per kilogram remain constant from birth through adolescence.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Requirements change substantially across the paediatric period, being highest per kg in early infancy.

answers.text: Energy requirements per kilogram peak at age 5 years when school-age activity increases.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The peak per-kilogram energy requirement is in early infancy, not school age, because of the metabolic demands of rapid growth and brain development.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the section on age-specific energy requirements. Infancy carries the highest per-kilogram demand due to rapid growth velocity.
Well done. Early infants have the highest per-kg energy needs — a key principle for counselling parents about feeding frequency.
